items.title: 4.9 Importance of stoichiometry in production and dosage of medicine

blocks.text: While preparing the required dose of a medicine, the optimum amount of the active ingredient is essential to produce the desired effects in the patient. Stoichiometry ensures the accuracy of drug synthesis: any deviation can result in an incomplete reaction or contamination with unreacted reactants or by-products. Stoichiometry lets chemists control chemical reactions precisely to produce drugs and to ensure their efficiency, effectiveness and safe use.

blocks.prompt: A tablet is made with slightly less of one reactant than the balanced equation requires. Using the ideas of this chapter, what can go wrong with the product?
blocks.explanation: That reactant becomes the limiting reactant, so less active ingredient forms than intended and the dose is low. The other reactant is left in excess and contaminates the product with unreacted material, which may itself be harmful. Only exact stoichiometric amounts give the correct amount of pure active ingredient.

items: The right dose needs the optimum amount of active ingredient; stoichiometry keeps drug synthesis accurate, avoiding incomplete reactions and contamination by unreacted reactants or by-products.
